description: checkout-api returning 5xx errors due to payments-db connection pool exhaustion during Black Friday traffic spike
root_cause: payments-db max_connections set to 20, insufficient for peak load. Connection pool depleted under sustained high-throughput checkout flow, causing all new payment requests to timeout.
resolution: Increased payments-db connection pool from 20 to 50, added PgBouncer connection pooler as middleware, implemented circuit breaker pattern on checkout-api side

description: order-service experiencing intermittent timeouts when querying payments-db during end-of-month batch processing
root_cause: End-of-month reconciliation batch job consumed 15 of 20 available connections for extended periods, starving real-time order queries. Batch and OLTP workloads competing for same connection pool.
resolution: Separated batch processing to read replica, reserved 5 connections exclusively for real-time queries using connection pool partitioning

description: notification-service memory leak after v1.8.0 deployment caused OOMKilled restarts every 30 minutes
root_cause: Version 1.8.0 introduced an email template caching layer that never evicted entries. Each unique email template was cached indefinitely, causing heap to grow linearly with request volume until OOM.
resolution: Rolled back to v1.7.3, fixed the cache to use LRU eviction with 500-entry cap, redeployed as v1.8.1 with memory monitoring alerts

description: user-service high CPU and degraded response times after v2.3.0 deployment with unoptimized database query
root_cause: New user search feature in v2.3.0 used a full table scan instead of indexed query for the /api/users/search endpoint. CPU spiked to 95% under normal traffic as the query was called on every keystroke.
resolution: Added composite index on (last_name, first_name, email), optimized query to use ILIKE with trigram index, added query timeout of 200ms

description: auth-service complete outage caused by redis-cache crash, cascading to all authenticated endpoints
root_cause: Redis maxmemory reached 4GB limit during a session storm (marketing campaign drove 3x normal signups). OOM killer terminated Redis process. auth-service had no fallback for session validation without Redis.
resolution: Increased Redis maxmemory to 8GB, implemented database-backed session fallback in auth-service, added Redis memory alerting at 70% and 85% thresholds

description: api-gateway elevated latency and intermittent 504 errors due to upstream CDN provider degradation
root_cause: CDN provider experienced routing issues in EU-West region, causing 40% of static asset requests to timeout. api-gateway health checks were passing (they hit /health, not CDN-dependent paths) masking the issue.
resolution: Waited for CDN provider resolution (2h), then implemented multi-CDN failover and added synthetic monitoring that tests CDN-dependent paths

description: checkout-api payment failures after configuration change reduced database query timeout from 5000ms to 500ms
root_cause: Operations team updated checkout-api config to reduce query timeout as part of a latency optimization initiative. The new 500ms timeout was too aggressive for complex payment verification queries that legitimately take 200-800ms under load.
resolution: Reverted timeout to 3000ms (compromise between old 5000ms and attempted 500ms), documented acceptable query time ranges per endpoint, added config change review requirement for timeout values

description: payments-db planned maintenance window caused 15-minute service degradation when failover took longer than expected
root_cause: Scheduled maintenance on primary payments-db node. Automatic failover to replica took 12 minutes instead of expected 30 seconds due to replication lag backlog. During failover, all write queries failed.
resolution: Implemented streaming replication monitoring, added pre-maintenance replication lag check (must be <100ms before proceeding), updated runbook with manual failover steps

description: Complete web-frontend outage when auth-service internal TLS certificate expired, breaking all inter-service HTTPS communication
root_cause: Internal TLS certificate for auth-service.internal expired after 1-year validity period. Certificate renewal was manual and no automated alerting existed for internal cert expiry. All services communicating with auth-service over mTLS immediately failed.
resolution: Renewed certificate manually (15 min to generate + deploy), implemented cert-manager for automatic renewal 30 days before expiry, added monitoring for all internal certificate expiry dates

description: auth-service intermittent 403 errors after IAM policy update restricted OAuth scope for service-to-service tokens
root_cause: Security team updated IAM policies to enforce least-privilege OAuth scopes. The change inadvertently removed the 'user:read' scope from service-to-service tokens used by checkout-api and user-service to call auth-service, causing sporadic 403 Forbidden errors.
resolution: Added missing 'user:read' scope back to service accounts, implemented policy-as-code review process requiring automated scope validation before IAM changes are applied

description: checkout-api duplicate payment charges due to race condition in idempotency key handling under high concurrency
root_cause: Idempotency key lookup and insert were not wrapped in a database transaction. Under high concurrency two identical checkout requests could both pass the duplicate check before either wrote the key, resulting in double charges.
resolution: Wrapped idempotency key check-and-insert in a serializable transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE, added a unique constraint on the idempotency_key column as a safety net

description: checkout-api returning 3xx redirect loop after CDN caching rule change propagated stale Location headers
root_cause: CDN team enabled aggressive caching on /checkout/* paths. A 301 redirect from the old /checkout/v1 to /checkout/v2 was cached at the CDN edge. When /checkout/v2 also returned a redirect (session-based), the browser bounced between the two indefinitely.
resolution: Added Cache-Control: no-store to all redirect responses, purged CDN cache for /checkout/* paths, documented redirect endpoints as non-cacheable

description: checkout-api memory pressure from unbounded in-memory cart session store during flash sale
root_cause: Cart sessions were held in-process memory with no TTL or size limit. A flash sale generated 50k concurrent carts, pushing heap to 3.8GB on a 4GB container. GC pauses exceeded 2s, causing health check failures and pod restarts.
resolution: Moved cart sessions to redis-cache with 30-minute TTL, set container memory request to 2GB with a 3GB limit, added heap usage metrics to Grafana

description: user-service connection leak to user-db caused pool exhaustion over 48 hours
root_cause: A code path in the password reset flow opened a database connection but did not close it when the user's email was not found (early return skipped the finally block). Connections leaked at ~2/minute, exhausting the pool after 48 hours.
resolution: Refactored all DB access to use context managers (with statement), added connection pool monitoring with alerts at 80% usage, deployed hotfix v2.4.1

description: user-service triggered a token refresh storm against auth-service after clock skew on 2 of 3 pods
root_cause: NTP sync failed on two user-service pods, causing their system clocks to drift 5 minutes ahead. JWT expiration checks used the local clock, so tokens appeared expired prematurely. Both pods refreshed tokens on every request, overwhelming auth-service with 800 req/s of token refreshes.
resolution: Restarted NTP daemon on affected pods, added clock skew tolerance of 30s to JWT validation, implemented token refresh rate limiting (max 1 refresh per token per 10s)

description: user-service profile update endpoint accepted malformed JSON payloads causing silent data corruption in user-db
root_cause: The PATCH /api/users/{id} endpoint used permissive JSON parsing that coerced invalid field types (e.g., integer phone numbers) without validation. Corrupted records caused downstream failures in notification-service when rendering templates with null-coerced fields.
resolution: Added strict Pydantic validation on all write endpoints, backfilled 340 corrupted records from audit log, deployed v2.5.2 with input sanitization

description: auth-service token blacklist propagation lag allowed revoked tokens to remain valid for up to 5 minutes
root_cause: Token blacklist was cached in redis-cache with a 5-minute TTL for performance. When a user's session was revoked (e.g., password change), the revocation did not invalidate the cache, so other pods continued to accept the old token until the cache entry expired.
resolution: Switched to a pub/sub invalidation model: revocation publishes to a Redis channel, all auth-service pods subscribe and immediately remove the token from their local cache

description: auth-service rate limiter misconfigured after deploy, blocking legitimate login attempts at 10 req/min instead of 100 req/min
root_cause: Deployment pipeline injected environment-specific config from a YAML file. A merge conflict in the staging config left the production rate_limit_per_minute at 10 (staging value) instead of 100. Deployed at 02:00, detected at 08:30 when US-East traffic started.
resolution: Corrected rate limit to 100 req/min, added config diff review as a mandatory deploy gate, added synthetic login monitoring that detects 429 responses within 5 minutes

description: auth-service intermittent failures during redis-cache sentinel failover triggered by network partition
root_cause: A brief network partition (90s) between Redis sentinel nodes caused a split-brain failover. Sentinels elected a new primary while the old primary was still accepting writes. auth-service clients split between the two primaries, causing inconsistent session reads and sporadic 500 errors.
resolution: Configured min-replicas-to-write=1 on Redis primary to prevent writes during partition, tuned sentinel down-after-milliseconds from 5000 to 15000 to avoid premature failovers, added sentinel topology monitoring

description: payments-db query performance degraded 10x over two weeks due to table bloat from missed autovacuum
root_cause: A long-running analytics query held a transaction open for 6 hours daily, preventing autovacuum from reclaiming dead tuples on the payments table. After two weeks the table had 80% dead rows, causing sequential scans on every index lookup.
resolution: Killed the long-running transaction, ran manual VACUUM FULL on the payments table (15 min downtime), moved analytics queries to a read replica, set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to 30 minutes

description: payments-db replication broke after SSL certificate renewal on primary did not propagate to replica
root_cause: SSL certificate was renewed on the primary payments-db node as part of quarterly rotation. The replica's pg_hba.conf required the old certificate fingerprint for replication connections. Replication stopped silently; detected 4 hours later when replica lag alert fired.
resolution: Updated replica pg_hba.conf with the new certificate, restarted replication, switched to certificate CN validation instead of fingerprint, added replication lag alerting at 1-minute threshold

description: order-service processed duplicate order events after Kafka consumer rebalance during deployment
root_cause: Rolling deployment restarted order-service pods one by one. Each restart triggered a Kafka consumer group rebalance. During rebalance, uncommitted offsets were replayed, causing 127 orders to be processed twice in a 10-minute window.
resolution: Implemented idempotent event processing with a deduplication table keyed on event_id, configured consumer group with cooperative-sticky assignor to minimize rebalance scope

description: order-service order confirmation flow stalled when notification-service was unreachable due to DNS resolution failure
root_cause: Internal DNS server had a stale record for notification-service.internal pointing to a decommissioned IP. order-service called notification-service synchronously in the order confirmation path with no timeout, causing order confirmations to hang indefinitely.
resolution: Fixed DNS record, made notification-service call asynchronous (fire-and-forget with retry queue), added 3s timeout to all inter-service HTTP calls, added DNS TTL monitoring

description: order-service payment verification failures after config change doubled the retry interval to payments-db
root_cause: A config change intended to reduce payments-db load doubled the retry backoff (from 500ms to 1000ms base). Combined with the existing 3-retry limit and 3s total timeout, payment verification now timed out on any query taking >1s, which was common during peak hours.
resolution: Reverted retry backoff to 500ms, increased total timeout to 5s, added circuit breaker with 50% error threshold to fast-fail instead of queueing retries

description: notification-service email delivery stopped after SMTP relay connection pool was exhausted by a bulk campaign
root_cause: Marketing triggered a 200k-recipient email campaign through the same SMTP relay used for transactional emails. The relay's 50-connection limit was consumed entirely by campaign emails, blocking order confirmation and password reset emails for 90 minutes.
resolution: Separated transactional and campaign email into different SMTP relays with independent connection pools, added priority queuing (transactional > campaign), set campaign send rate to 500/min

description: notification-service crash loop after template rendering hit a null pointer on orders missing a shipping address
root_cause: Order confirmation template referenced {{order.shipping_address.city}} without null checking. Digital-only orders have no shipping address. v1.9.2 deployment added digital orders to the confirmation flow without updating the template, causing a NullPointerException on every digital order notification.
resolution: Added null-safe template rendering with default values, backfilled failed notifications for 89 affected orders, added template rendering unit tests for all order types

description: web-frontend load time regressed from 2s to 12s after v4.1.0 bundled an unminified analytics library
root_cause: v4.1.0 added a third-party analytics SDK. The developer imported the debug build (2.3MB) instead of the production build (180KB). The bundle size increase was not caught because the CI pipeline had no bundle size budget.
resolution: Swapped to the production analytics build, added webpack-bundle-analyzer to CI with a 500KB per-chunk budget, page load returned to 1.8s

description: web-frontend serving stale content after CDN cache poisoning via manipulated Host header
root_cause: CDN cached responses keyed by URL path only, not by Host header. An attacker sent requests with a manipulated Host header pointing to a malicious origin, and the CDN cached the response. Subsequent legitimate users received the cached malicious content.
resolution: Configured CDN to include Host header in cache key, added Vary: Host to all origin responses, purged entire CDN cache, enabled WAF rule to reject requests with non-whitelisted Host headers

description: web-frontend users logged out repeatedly after auth-service session format changed in a backward-incompatible upgrade
root_cause: auth-service v3.1.0 changed the session token format from opaque to JWT. web-frontend's session middleware still expected the opaque format and rejected all new tokens as invalid, forcing re-login. Old sessions worked until they expired.
resolution: Updated web-frontend session middleware to accept both formats, added backward-compatibility tests to auth-service CI, implemented a session migration endpoint

description: api-gateway TLS handshake timeouts to upstream services after OpenSSL library update in base image
root_cause: Base Docker image update pulled OpenSSL 3.1 which deprecated certain cipher suites still used by upstream services. TLS handshakes fell back to a slower negotiation path, adding 800ms per request. Under load, the handshake queue backed up and connections timed out.
resolution: Pinned OpenSSL to 3.0.x in the Dockerfile, scheduled cipher suite upgrade across all services for the next maintenance window, added TLS handshake latency to monitoring dashboards

description: api-gateway rate limiting blocked all traffic after production config was overwritten with staging values
root_cause: Infrastructure-as-code pipeline had a misconfigured environment selector. A staging deployment also applied the staging rate-limit config (5 req/s global) to the production api-gateway. All production traffic beyond 5 req/s was rejected with 429.
resolution: Reverted config to production values (10000 req/s), fixed environment selector in pipeline, added environment-name validation that rejects staging configs on production resources

description: api-gateway routing loop between canary and stable deployments caused 50% of requests to fail with 502
root_cause: Canary deployment of api-gateway v3.9.5 had a routing rule that forwarded unknown paths back to the ingress controller. The ingress controller routed them back to the canary based on traffic splitting weight, creating an infinite loop that exhausted the request hop limit.
resolution: Fixed canary routing to return 404 for unknown paths instead of forwarding, added max-forwards header check, limited canary traffic to 5% during initial rollout

description: redis-cache eviction storm under memory pressure caused auth-service session lookup latency to spike 20x
root_cause: Redis reached 95% of maxmemory (3.8GB of 4GB). allkeys-lru eviction kicked in aggressively, evicting 50k keys/second including active session tokens. auth-service had to re-validate sessions against user-db on every evicted key, adding 15ms per request.
resolution: Increased maxmemory to 6GB, separated session keys into a dedicated Redis database with volatile-lru policy, added memory usage alerting at 70% threshold

description: redis-cache cluster split-brain after network partition between availability zones caused data inconsistency
root_cause: Network partition between AZ-1 and AZ-2 lasted 3 minutes. Redis Sentinel in AZ-2 promoted a replica to primary. When the partition healed, two primaries existed briefly. Writes during the split were lost when the old primary demoted itself and synced from the new primary.
resolution: Configured min-replicas-to-write=1 and min-replicas-max-lag=10 to prevent writes during partitions, added cross-AZ network monitoring, documented data loss window in SLA

description: user-db lock contention on the users table caused cascading timeouts in user-service and auth-service
root_cause: A schema migration added a NOT NULL column with a DEFAULT value to the 2M-row users table. PostgreSQL acquired an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the ALTER TABLE, blocking all reads and writes for 45 seconds. Connection queues on user-service and auth-service filled up, causing cascading 503s.
resolution: Reverted migration, re-applied using a three-step safe pattern (add nullable column, backfill in batches, set NOT NULL), added pg_stat_activity monitoring for long-running DDL

description: user-db migration renamed the email column breaking backward compatibility with user-service v2.4.x still in canary
root_cause: Database migration renamed 'email' to 'email_address' as part of a schema cleanup. user-service v2.5.0 expected the new name, but the canary deployment still had 20% traffic on v2.4.x which queried the old column name, causing SELECT failures.
resolution: Added a database view aliasing email_address back to email, completed canary rollout to 100% v2.5.0, dropped the view after confirming no queries used the old name

description: user-db replication lag spiked to 30 minutes after a bulk data import for GDPR compliance filled the WAL
root_cause: A GDPR compliance script imported 500k anonymized records into user-db in a single transaction. The WAL (write-ahead log) grew to 12GB, and the replica could not keep up with the replay. During the 30-minute lag window, read replicas served stale data to user-service.
resolution: Broke future bulk imports into 10k-row batches with 1s pauses between commits, set max_wal_size to 4GB with alerting at 2GB, added replica lag monitoring visible on the SRE dashboard

description: cdn-provider origin pull failures caused api-gateway to serve 502 errors on all static asset routes
root_cause: CDN provider rotated their origin-pull TLS certificates but did not update the certificate pinning on their edge nodes. Origin pulls from EU and APAC edges failed TLS validation. NA edges used a different certificate chain and were unaffected.
resolution: CDN provider deployed the updated certificate pins to all edges (2h resolution). Added origin-pull health check from multiple regions, negotiated SLA credit for the outage

description: cdn-provider wildcard SSL certificate renewal delayed by 48 hours, causing browser security warnings on web-frontend
root_cause: CDN provider's automated certificate renewal failed due to a DNS validation issue on the wildcard domain. The renewal retry was scheduled for 24h later. The certificate expired before the retry succeeded, triggering browser SSL warnings for all web-frontend users.
resolution: CDN provider manually renewed the certificate (3h after escalation). Switched to HTTP-01 validation as primary with DNS-01 as fallback, added certificate expiry monitoring with 7-day and 24-hour alerts

description: checkout-api payment webhook processing fell behind after payments-db connection pool saturated during a promotional event
root_cause: Payment provider webhook callbacks spiked 10x during a promotional event. Each webhook handler opened a new database connection to verify and record the payment status. The connection pool (20 connections) saturated in under a minute, causing webhook deliveries to timeout and be retried, creating a feedback loop.
resolution: Implemented webhook ingestion queue (Redis-backed), decoupled webhook receipt from database writes, increased connection pool to 50 with connection timeout of 5s

description: order-service data inconsistency after ETL pipeline wrote directly to payments-db bypassing application-level validation
root_cause: The nightly ETL pipeline for financial reporting connected directly to payments-db and ran UPDATE statements to mark reconciled orders. A bug in the ETL query used order_id instead of payment_id in the WHERE clause, updating 230 unrelated payment records with incorrect reconciliation status.
resolution: Reverted the 230 records from the audit log, restricted ETL pipeline to read-only replica access, implemented all payment status changes through the checkout-api REST endpoint

description: api-gateway health checks passing while checkout-api was partially degraded, masking payment failures for 25 minutes
root_cause: api-gateway health check endpoint (/health) tested connectivity to upstream services with a simple ping. checkout-api responded to pings normally but its payment processing path was broken due to a deadlocked thread pool. Health checks passed, so the load balancer continued routing traffic.
resolution: Changed health checks to deep checks that exercise critical paths (checkout-api /health now verifies a test payment flow), added separate liveness and readiness probes with different check depths

description: notification-service sending duplicate order confirmation emails after redis-cache failover lost the deduplication set
root_cause: notification-service used a Redis SET to track sent notification IDs for deduplication. During a scheduled Redis maintenance failover, the replica had 30s of replication lag. All notification IDs written in that window were lost. The retry queue re-processed those notifications as new, sending 4200 duplicate emails.
resolution: Added a deduplication table in a persistent store (user-db) as the source of truth, used Redis only as a fast-path cache with 1h TTL, added duplicate detection in the email provider callback

description: user-service search endpoint returned results from deleted accounts due to missing soft-delete filter in the new search query
root_cause: The v2.5.0 user search rewrite used a new Elasticsearch index for performance. The indexing pipeline did not filter out soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). 1200 deleted accounts appeared in search results, including accounts deleted for GDPR compliance.
resolution: Added deleted_at filter to the Elasticsearch indexing pipeline, purged deleted accounts from the index, added a nightly reconciliation job that verifies index-to-database consistency

description: payments-db standby promotion during maintenance exposed a 2-hour replication slot bloat that prevented WAL cleanup
root_cause: A dormant replication slot from a decommissioned analytics replica prevented WAL segment cleanup for 2 hours during maintenance. When the standby was promoted, it replayed WAL from the slot's retained position, adding 2 hours of catch-up time and blocking all writes during replay.
resolution: Dropped the orphaned replication slot, added monitoring for inactive replication slots (alert if any slot has >100MB of retained WAL), documented slot lifecycle in the runbook

description: web-frontend checkout flow broken after api-gateway deployed a CORS policy change that blocked cross-origin requests from the SPA
root_cause: api-gateway v3.9.3 tightened CORS policy to only allow requests from the primary domain. The SPA was served from a CDN subdomain (static.example.com) not included in the new allowlist. All API calls from the frontend were blocked by the browser's CORS preflight.
resolution: Added the CDN subdomain to the CORS allowlist, added automated CORS validation tests that verify the SPA domain is always permitted, added CORS error monitoring on the frontend

description: auth-service JWT validation failures after clock drift between auth-service pods and user-service caused 'token not yet valid' errors
root_cause: auth-service issued JWTs with nbf (not-before) set to the issuing pod's clock time. Two auth-service pods had clocks 45 seconds ahead of user-service pods. Tokens issued by those pods were rejected by user-service as 'not yet valid' for the first 45 seconds of their lifetime.
resolution: Deployed chrony NTP synchronization across all pods, added 60-second clock skew tolerance to JWT validation, added clock drift monitoring with 10-second alert threshold
